title: Who made whom?
goal: Say who made someone do something, with the accusative or the dative: Çocuğu güldürdü, Raporu Ali'ye yazdırdım.

intro.text: From a verb without an object, the one you make act takes the accusative: *Bebeği uyuttum* (I put the baby to sleep). From a verb with an object, that person goes in the dative: *Raporu Ali'ye yazdırdım* (I had Ali write the report).

vocab.en: to lift, to raise; to remove

exercises.question: *Bebek uyudu.* Which sentence means **I put the baby to sleep**?

why.1: *Uyumak* has no object, so the baby becomes the object of *uyutmak*, in the accusative: *bebeği*.
why.2: The baby is a definite object here: it needs the accusative *bebeği*.

exercises.explain: *uyu-t-tu-m*: the one who sleeps becomes the object, *bebek* + *-i*, with k softened to ğ.

exercises.en: I had Ali write the report.

reject.why: *Raporu* is already the object. With a verb that has one, the person made to act goes in the dative: *Ali'ye*.

exercises.explain: The report keeps its accusative; Ali, who does the writing, takes the dative `-(y)A`.
*gül-* has one syllable, so the causative is `-DIr`, here *-dür*: *gül-dür-dü*. *-t* is only for longer stems.

reject.why: *Korkmak* has no object, so the person you frighten is the object of *korkutmak*, in the accusative: *beni*.

exercises.en: This news made me very happy.

accept: My father does not let anyone drive his car.
My [father|dad] does not let anybody drive his car.
My dad does not let anyone drive his car.
My [father|dad] does not let anyone use his car.
My [father|dad] [lets nobody|never lets anyone|will not let anyone] [drive|use] his car.

exercises.prompt: The clown made the children laugh.

exercises.en: My mother fed the baby some soup.
exercises.explain: *Yemek* has a one-syllable stem, so its causative is *ye-dir-*: **to feed**. *Çorba* is the object, so the baby, who eats, goes in the dative: *bebeğe*.

reject.why: The one kept waiting is the object of *bekletmek*, in the accusative: *beni bekletme*.

exercises.question: *Annem bana odamı toplattı.* Who tidied the room?

why.1: Your mother is the subject of the causative: she made someone else do it.
why.2: Nothing says you worked together; *bana* marks the one who was made to tidy.

exercises.explain: *topla-t-tı*: the dative *bana* is the person made to do it, **my mother made me tidy my room**.

accept: Thanks for reminding me of my appointment.
Thank you for reminding me [of|about] my appointment.
Thanks for reminding me about my appointment.

exercises.prompt: Who woke you up so early?
accept: Seni bu kadar erken kim uyandırdı?
Sizi bu kadar erken kim uyandırdı?

reject.answer: Seni bu kadar erken kim uyandı?
reject.why: *Uyanmak* is **to wake up** yourself. To wake someone else, use the causative: *uyan-dır-dı*.

exercises.en: The police officer stopped the car.

reject.why: *Durmak* has no object: *Araba durdu* (the car stopped). To stop something, use the causative: *dur-dur-du*.

exercises.explain: *dur-* has one syllable, so the causative is `-DIr`: *durdur-*, then the past *-du*.
